meta.author: separate case-author subagent
meta.notes: Wrote 3 practice and 16 test cases in 19 distinct fictional, mundane domains, varying claim types (occurrence, threshold, cause, attribution, completion) with 5 of 19 phrased negatively. Each e1 is a single preliminary or partial account with stated limitations, and each e2 comes from a different fictional organization using a different method, adds moderate support with its own limitation, and never mentions e1.

cases.claim: The Tavrenmoor street lighting crew completed lamp replacements on all 18 streetlight poles along Ostler Lane by 15 April 2026.

e1.source: Tavrenmoor Street Services weekly works bulletin
e1.text: The weekly works bulletin lists the Ostler Lane lamp replacement order as closed on 14 April. Crew supervisor Dorit Haskell reported by radio that the last fittings went in that afternoon. The bulletin is compiled from supervisors' own reports and is not checked against site visits, and the closure entry does not record how many poles were actually serviced. Two other lighting orders closed this quarter were later reopened after residents reported poles still dark.

e2.text: On the evening of 19 April, six members of the residents group walked the full length of Ostler Lane during their regular neighbourhood safety walk. They counted 18 lit streetlights between the primary school gate and the canal footbridge, with no dark poles. The group does not track maintenance work and has no record of when individual lamps were changed, and one lamp near number 61 flickered for several seconds before settling.

cases.claim: A swarm left hive 12 at the Callowen Hill community apiary on 3 June 2026.

e1.source: Callowen Hill Community Apiary inspection log
e1.text: At the routine inspection on 4 June, volunteer keeper Anselm Rudd recorded hive 12 as much quieter than the neighbouring hives, with several capped queen cells on the upper frames and no sighting of the marked queen. Rain cut the inspection short before the lower brood box was examined, so the queen may have been present and simply missed. An allotment holder next to the site said she saw a large number of bees in the air on the afternoon of 3 June but could not say which hive they came from.

e2.source: Larchwyn Hive Telemetry monthly data summary
e2.text: The remote scale fitted under hive 12 at the Callowen Hill site logged an abrupt weight loss of about 1.7 kilograms between 13:40 and 14:00 on 3 June, with no matching change at the other two monitored hives. A sharp midday drop of this size is typical of a departing swarm, although a similar step can occur when frames or a super are removed, and the telemetry service holds no record of whether anyone opened the hive that day.

cases.claim: Dravelin Parcels made no delivery attempt for parcel 44-7712 at Flat 3, Pellow Court, in Halbreth on 12 March 2026.

e1.source: Dravelin Parcels customer service case note
e1.text: The handheld scan for parcel 44-7712 was logged as an attempted delivery with no answer at 14:12 on 12 March, but the location stamp on that scan places the device about 2.4 kilometres from Pellow Court, on the depot side of the ring road. Location stamps in central Halbreth are sometimes wrong by a kilometre or more when the handheld loses its satellite fix, and the driver has not yet been interviewed. The recipient says she was at home all afternoon and found no calling card.

e2.source: Pellow Court Management Company entry log review
e2.text: The door entry panel at Pellow Court logged no calls to Flat 3 and no use of the trade access code between 12:00 and 17:00 on 12 March. Lobby camera footage for the same period, reviewed by the building manager, shows no one in courier uniform entering. The panel does not record entries through the rear bin-store door, which residents sometimes leave unlatched, and the camera does not cover that route.

cases.claim: Turbidity in the combined filtered water leaving the Kestermoor water treatment works rose above 1.0 NTU on 9 February 2026.

e1.source: Kestermoor Treatment Works shift operator log
e1.text: At 02:15 on 9 February the online turbidity meter on the combined filter outlet at Kestermoor showed a short rise, peaking at a displayed 1.3 NTU before falling below 0.5 NTU within about 25 minutes. The rise followed the return to service of a freshly backwashed filter, which can briefly release particles. Night operator Halvard Brenn noted that the meter had been cleaned the previous afternoon and that trapped air after cleaning can produce false spikes. No grab sample was taken during the rise, so the displayed peak has not been verified.

e2.source: Ellisford Water Networks distribution monitoring note
e2.text: The turbidity monitor at the Harl Street service reservoir inlet, which receives water only from the Kestermoor works, recorded a rise to 0.9 NTU at about 03:40 on 9 February, against a usual level below 0.2 NTU. Travel time from the works to Harl Street is normally around 80 minutes. Mixing and settling in the trunk main generally lower peaks before they reach the inlet, although a valve operation on the main the previous evening may also have stirred up sediment.

cases.claim: The cracks found in the east abutment of the Varrow Creek road bridge in March 2026 were caused by a seized expansion bearing.

e1.source: Quorran County Highways bridge inspection note
e1.text: A visual inspection of the Varrow Creek road bridge on 17 March found three diagonal cracks in the east abutment seat, the widest about 2 millimetres. Inspector Odile Faverly observed that the east expansion bearing was heavily corroded and that its sliding plate appeared to sit hard against its end stop, which would push thermal movement into the abutment. The bearing could only be viewed from the riverbank through binoculars because the access platform was unavailable, and the inspector noted that settlement of the abutment footing had not been ruled out.

e2.text: Displacement gauges fitted across the east bearing of the Varrow Creek bridge from 20 March to 1 April recorded almost no horizontal movement while deck temperatures swung by about 14 degrees Celsius, whereas the west bearing moved freely over the same period. Crack-width gauges on the east abutment showed small openings on the warmest afternoons, close to the limit of their resolution. Level surveys found no measurable settlement of the abutment, though a two-week record is short and covers only spring temperatures.

cases.claim: The checkout outage at Pelloway Commerce on 14 May 2026 was not caused by the database failover that happened earlier that morning.

e1.text: Pelloway's primary order database failed over to its standby at 06:52, and checkout errors began at 07:31. The on-call engineer, Rafe Annersley, noted that order writes resumed normally within two minutes of the failover and that error rates stayed flat for the following half hour. He suspects an expired certificate on the payment gateway connector instead, but these notes were written during the incident, before logs from all services had been collected, and a delayed effect of the failover on connection pools has not been excluded.

e2.text: Halvane Payments gateway logs show that from 07:29 to 08:46 on 14 May, connection attempts from merchants still presenting certificates under a retired intermediate authority were refused at the handshake stage, following a scheduled certificate rotation. Pelloway Commerce was among the merchants with refused handshakes throughout that window. The gateway team has no view of merchants' internal systems, so it cannot say whether other faults were also affecting Pelloway's checkout at the time.

cases.claim: Speckled fen newts bred in Pond 4 at the Ashlar Moss nature reserve during spring 2026.

e1.source: Ashlar Moss Reserve volunteer survey sheet
e1.text: During a torchlight survey of Pond 4 at Ashlar Moss on the night of 21 April, volunteer surveyor Marguerite Osei counted two adult speckled fen newts, one of them a male in breeding crest. She also found a single folded leaf of the kind females use to wrap eggs, but could not open it without damaging it, so no egg was seen. Water clarity was poor, only the northern margin was searchable, and adults are known to visit ponds without breeding in them.

e2.source: Westerlaine Amphibian Recording Group netting report
e2.text: Standardised dip-netting of Pond 4 at Ashlar Moss on 9 July produced three newt larvae with the pale flank spotting typical of speckled fen newts, alongside many larvae of the grey newt. The larvae were photographed and released. Pond 4 has no inflow from other water bodies, so larvae are unlikely to have been washed in. At this stage the two species can be confused, and the photographs have not yet been checked by the county recorder.

cases.claim: More than 40 of the 2,000 hinge brackets in Merrovale Metalworks lot 3317 had hole spacing outside the drawing tolerance.

e1.source: Merrovale Metalworks press line quality check sheet
e1.text: Of 50 hinge brackets pulled from lot 3317 for the end-of-shift check, two had hole spacing outside the drawing tolerance of plus or minus 0.15 millimetres, one of them only just beyond the limit. Both came from the final tray, produced after a die change. Quality technician Bram Tollefsen recorded that the check gauge's pins were worn and due for replacement, which can make borderline parts read as failures, and that a sample of this size gives only a rough indication of the lot as a whole.

e2.text: Goods-in staff at Kessling Cabinetry measured 120 hinge brackets drawn at random from the 2,000 delivered as Merrovale lot 3317, using a coordinate measuring arm rather than a go/no-go gauge. Three brackets had hole spacing outside the drawing tolerance and two more were within 0.01 millimetres of the limit. The measuring arm was last calibrated eight months ago, and brackets from different trays had been mixed together in the delivery crates, so the sample may not represent each tray equally.

cases.claim: The oak posts found in Trench 2 at the Kilvarren Fields excavation were felled before AD 1100.

e1.source: Kilvarren Fields Excavation interim site diary
e1.text: The two oak posts uncovered in Trench 2 at Kilvarren Fields sit in a cut sealed beneath a clay floor containing pottery of a type that, in this district, generally went out of use during the eleventh century. Site director Juniper Malvray considers the posts part of the earliest building phase. The pottery sample is small, about a dozen sherds, and some could have been brought up from earlier layers by later disturbance, so the floor may be younger than the sherds suggest. Wood samples have been sent for dating but no results have been received.

e2.text: A ring-width sequence of 112 years from the better-preserved Kilvarren Fields post cross-matched the regional oak reference chronology, giving an outermost ring of AD 1052. Six sapwood rings survived but not the bark edge, and applying the regional sapwood estimate gives a felling range of AD 1061 to 1094. The cross-match was only moderately strong and has not been replicated, because the second post had too few rings to measure, and oaks from waterlogged sites sometimes carry more sapwood than the regional estimate allows.

cases.claim: Tressick Agri Services did not complete the second fungicide spray on field 9 at Corvane Farm before rain began on 22 May 2026.

e1.text: Farm manager Selin Marrack noted that at about 15:30 on 22 May the contractor's sprayer was applying the second fungicide spray near the middle of field 9, with fresh wheel marks visible only on the western tramlines. Heavy rain began at about 16:00. A large part of the field appeared unsprayed when she passed, but she saw it only briefly from the road, did not see the sprayer leave, and did not walk the field afterwards. Wheel marks are hard to judge from a distance.

e2.text: The application record downloaded from the sprayer's control unit shows the boom active over 11.4 of the 18.6 hectares of field 9 at Corvane Farm during the fungicide job on 22 May, with spraying stopping at 15:51 and the machine leaving the field at 16:06. No further application on field 9 is logged that week. The unit had two logging dropouts earlier in May, and coverage near the woodland on the eastern side is often under-recorded when satellite reception is poor.

cases.claim: The bulk carrier MV Orrin Lark did not discharge ballast water inside the Quillon Bay no-discharge zone on 2 August 2026.

e1.source: Quillon Bay Port Authority harbour patrol report
e1.text: After a fishing skipper reported discoloured water around the bulk carrier MV Orrin Lark on 2 August, while the ship lay at anchor in the part of Quillon Bay where ballast discharge is banned, a patrol launch reached it at 11:20 and watched its hull for about 20 minutes. The launch crew saw no outflow from any overboard opening, and the discoloured patch appeared to be drifting from the river mouth. The launch arrived roughly 40 minutes after the report, so a discharge that had already stopped could have been missed, and no water samples were taken.

e2.text: Surveyors from Marrowind Marine Surveys boarded the MV Orrin Lark on 4 August. The ballast pump run-hour counters and the ballast treatment system's flow log showed no ballast operations between 30 July and 4 August, and soundings of all ballast tanks were within 40 tonnes of the figures recorded when the ship left its previous port. Soundings at that accuracy could not detect a small release, and water draining by gravity through the sea chest would not register on the pump counters.

cases.claim: The low-speed derailment of tram 214 at the Tolcaster Tramways depot on 6 September 2026 was caused by a worn switch blade.

e1.text: Tram 214 derailed its leading bogie at walking pace while entering the Tolcaster Tramways depot over points 7 at 22:48 on 6 September. No one was hurt. Depot supervisor Corin Ellery found a chipped and visibly worn tip on the left switch blade, with wheel climb marks starting just beyond it. The tram's wheel profiles have not yet been measured, and the driver's account of the approach speed has not been checked against the onboard recorder, so a wheel defect or overspeed remains possible.

e2.text: Wheel profile measurements on tram 214 taken on 10 September found all wheels within limits, although the left leading flange was close to the thin end of the permitted range. The onboard recorder download shows a speed of 7 kilometres per hour over points 7 at the depot entrance, below the 10 kilometres per hour limit. The switch blade at points 7 had already been replaced and scrapped before the visit, so its condition could not be examined directly.

cases.claim: The internal temperature of ultra-low freezer F-3 at the Harwen Biosciences sample store rose above minus 60 degrees Celsius during the power cut on 11 July 2026.

e1.text: Mains power to the Harwen Biosciences sample store was lost from 00:20 to 04:40 on 11 July, and the standby generator failed to start. When technician Nadia Kostell arrived at 04:55, the door display on freezer F-3 read minus 63 degrees Celsius and was dropping as the compressor recovered, so the unit had been warmer before she arrived. The display shows only the current value, and the freezer's internal data logger had a flat battery, so the peak temperature during the outage was not recorded.

e2.source: Ambrel Clinical Trials sample custody memo
e2.text: Five sample boxes held by Ambrel Clinical Trials in freezer F-3 at Harwen Biosciences each carry an irreversible indicator label that turns red after exposure above minus 60 degrees Celsius. On retrieval on 13 July, three of the five labels had turned red, all on boxes from the upper two shelves. The labels are rated to within about two degrees of their stated threshold, and boxes on upper shelves warm faster than the cabinet as a whole.

cases.claim: The feeder isolator found open at the Senlow Road substation on 19 March 2026 had been opened by a crew from the contractor Corbrin Electrical.

e1.text: When a Velmark Power responder reached the Senlow Road substation at 11:30 on 19 March, he found the feeder isolator open and a Corbrin Electrical crew connecting metering cables to that feeder inside the compound. No Velmark switching had been scheduled there that day, and the crew's work order did not authorise any. The Corbrin foreman said his crew had not touched the switchgear, and the compound gate had been left unlocked for part of the morning, so someone else may have entered the site.

e2.source: Tamsett Cold Storage security footage review
e2.text: A security camera at Tamsett Cold Storage, which overlooks the Senlow Road substation compound from across the road, recorded two people in orange high-visibility clothing entering the switchgear room at 10:37 on 19 March and leaving at 10:44. A white van with a blue roof stripe, similar to vehicles in the Corbrin Electrical fleet, was parked by the gate throughout. The footage is low resolution, faces and lettering cannot be read, and the camera does not show inside the switchgear room.

cases.claim: The 14 pallets sent to the wrong customer from the Ennersby Logistics warehouse at Drummel Park on 27 April 2026 were picked by the night shift.

e1.source: Ennersby Logistics Drummel Park shift manager note
e1.text: The warehouse system attributes all 14 pallet picks for the order that went to the wrong customer on 27 April to scanner logins held by two night-shift pickers. Shift manager Imre Halloran pointed out that handheld scanners are often passed between shifts without the previous user logging out, and the individual pick timestamps were overwritten when the order record was corrected later that day, so the system cannot show when the pallets were picked. The two pickers have not yet been asked about the order.

e2.text: Trailer tracking and the driver's log kept by Sarrowby Haulage show its trailer for the misdirected Ennersby order arriving at dock 6 of the Drummel Park warehouse at 03:05 on 27 April and leaving sealed with 14 pallets aboard at 04:20, before the warehouse day shift began at 06:00. The driver noted that the pallets were already wrapped and waiting on the dock when he arrived. The haulier's records cannot show when the pallets were picked, and loads are sometimes staged on the dock from the previous afternoon.

cases.claim: The cooling-tunnel alarm on packing line 2 at the Tessaline Foods plant was acknowledged at 03:14 on 8 July 2026 by operator Ewan Pardley.

e1.source: Tessaline Foods night shift incident note
e1.text: The line 2 control panel logged the cooling-tunnel high-temperature alarm as acknowledged at 03:14, and the line 2 check sheet carries Ewan Pardley's initials against a tunnel temperature check at 03:20. All packing-line panels share one operator login, so the log cannot show who pressed the button, and check sheets are often filled in later in the shift. Night supervisor Lena Okafor noted that two other operators covered breaks on line 2 between 02:30 and 04:00.

e2.source: Kelvara Security Services access control report
e2.text: Badge records for the hygiene door into the line 2 packing hall at the Tessaline Foods plant show Ewan Pardley entering at 03:02 and leaving at 03:41 on 8 July, with no other badge used at that door between 02:55 and 03:45. Badges of the other two staff rostered to line 2 that night were used at the canteen door at 03:05 and 03:08. The hygiene door is sometimes held open for trolleys, so a person could pass through without badging.

cases.claim: The 24-hour mean PM10 concentration at the Tennick Road monitoring station in Calvenford did not exceed 50 micrograms per cubic metre on 3 October 2026.

e1.source: Calvenford Borough Council air quality bulletin
e1.text: Provisional data from the Tennick Road monitor gave a 24-hour mean PM10 concentration of 44 micrograms per cubic metre for 3 October, a day of bonfire smoke and light winds. Hourly readings peaked at 118 micrograms per cubic metre at around 21:00. The daily figure has not been ratified, and the monitor's heated inlet was replaced on 1 October; readings from newly fitted inlets have sometimes run low until they settle in. Ratified figures are normally issued about three months after measurement.

e2.source: Calven Valley Clean Air Partnership sensor network summary
e2.text: Seven low-cost optical sensors run by the Calven Valley Clean Air Partnership within 800 metres of Tennick Road gave 24-hour PM10 means for 3 October of between 31 and 47 micrograms per cubic metre, with the nearest unit reading 41. Sensors of this kind can be off by a wide margin in either direction and are not used for compliance reporting, and two of the seven went offline during the evening, when smoke was heaviest.

cases.claim: The fish kill at Lunmere Reservoir in August 2026 was caused by low dissolved oxygen following an algal bloom.

e1.text: Ranger Tomas Reyne counted roughly 300 dead fish along the eastern shore of Lunmere Reservoir on the morning of 14 August, after several hot, still days during which the water had turned a dense green. A handheld meter read 2.1 milligrams per litre of dissolved oxygen at the surface near the inflow at 07:30. Only one spot was measured, the meter was last calibrated in spring, and a farm slurry store upstream has leaked in previous summers, so a pollution incident cannot yet be excluded.

e2.source: Tarnwick Fish Health Laboratory examination summary
e2.text: Six fish collected by laboratory staff from Lunmere Reservoir on 14 August were examined. Gill tissue showed changes typical of oxygen starvation, with no lesions suggesting toxic chemical exposure or infection. Water samples from three points showed high chlorophyll and low ammonia, which does not fit organic pollution such as a sewage or farm waste discharge. The fish had been dead for some hours before collection, which limits what tissue examination can show, and the water samples were taken two days after the deaths.

cases.claim: Ferrowline Networks crews finished repairing the severed fibre cable on Pellam Road in Ostrevale before 06:00 on 21 January 2026.

e1.text: At 05:20 on 21 January the splicing team leader, Hessa Morland, radioed that the last of the 144 fibres in the damaged Pellam Road cable had been joined and that the team was closing the joint enclosure. Testing of the repaired fibres had not started at that point, and the dispatch desk has no further update from the site before the shift handover at 06:00. Repairs of this size sometimes need fibres re-spliced after testing shows high loss at a joint.

e2.text: Network monitoring at Tessmark Broadband, which leases fibres in the Pellam Road cable, shows its 12 circuits on that route coming back into service between 05:41 and 05:52 on 21 January, with error rates back to normal by 06:10. The monitoring covers only Tessmark's own fibres, and circuits are sometimes restored over temporary links before a permanent repair is finished.
